title: New MemGhost Attack Plants Persistent False Memories in AI Agents Through One Email
summary: Give an AI assistant a memory and access to your inbox, and you hand an attacker a way to rewrite what it thinks it knows about you. A single email can trick that agent into saving a false "fact" about the user, hide the change, and quietly steer its answers in later sessions.

title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued a postmortem on a recent data leak in which a contractor published dozens of internal CISA credentials including AWS Govcloud keys in a public GitHub repository for almost six months before being notified by KrebsOnSecurity. Experts say the gaps identified in the agency s initial response provide important lessons that all...

sections.overview: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued a postmortem on a recent data leak in which a contractor published dozens of internal CISA credentials including AWS Govcloud keys in a public GitHub repository for almost six months before being notified by KrebsOnSecurity. Experts say the gaps identified in the agency s initial response provide important lessons that all...
sections.technical: In CISA s case, these channels were not well defined, leading the security researcher to try multiple avenues – including emailing the contractor, submitting through CISA’s vulnerability disclosure platform (which is intended for vulnerabilities impacting the broader cybersecurity community), and ultimately involving a reporter, reads the analysis written by Preston Werntz and Brad Libbey , the acting chief information officer and acting chief information security officer at CISA, respectively. Put reporting instructions in several prominent places, and make sure a report about your own infrastructure does not land in a product-bug queue.
sections.impact:
CISA said those detailed logs allowed it to show that no customer or mission data was exposed, and that the leaked credentials were not used outside of CISA s environments. The postmortem stresses that clear and distinct reporting channels are essential to ensure that incidents affecting the organization itself are handled differently from those involving its products or customers. One of the exposed files, titled “importantAWStokens,” included the administrative credentials to three Amazon AWS GovCloud servers.

Assessed severity: HIGH.
sections.mitigation: The report s authors also emphasized the importance of continuously scanning public code repositories like GitHub for exposed secrets, and said CISA has since rotated all secrets and created an action plan to improve management of developer secrets and to better monitor for them going forward. Experts say the gaps identified in the agency s initial response provide important lessons that all security teams should absorb. Continuous monitoring of public GitHub surfaced it. Comprehensive internal scanning could have caught the plaintext passwords and committed backups long before they left the building.
sections.context: This fits the broader data-exposure trend where follow-on abuse of leaked information is common.

email_summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued a postmortem on a recent data leak in which a contractor published dozens of internal CISA credentials including AWS Govcloud keys in a public GitHub repository for almost six months before being notified by KrebsOnSecurity. Severity is rated high.

title: Misconfigured Server Reveals Three Evilginx Phishing Operations Targeting Microsoft 365
